title: Elmo QA Sort: All 41 Recurring Pains
summary: Cross-reference of all 41 recurring Corner pains against Elmo QA findings: which failures are real vs invented, what still has zero QA coverage, and priority order for Bobby.
content:
Elmo QA Sort: All 41 Recurring Pains

Author: Steve (Sales Director) Date: 2026-03-23 Method: Cross-reference every item in projects/sys/patrik-recurring-pains.md against Elmo's world switcher QA findings. Verdict: REAL = in Patrik's exact words. INVENTED = Steve or Elmo added it. CANNOT CONFIRM = status unclear from available data.

Scope Note

Elmo ran one QA pass so far: the world switcher dropdown (35 checks, 19 PASS, 9 FAIL, 8 CANNOT TEST).

The 41 recurring pains cover the full dashboard experience. Most of the 41 were NOT in scope for Elmo's world switcher pass. This sort maps which of the 9 FAIL items align with Patrik's stated pains, and which of the 41 pains still have zero QA coverage.

Section A: Elmo's 9 FAIL Items -- Real vs Invented

FAIL #1: No separator between Preferences and Create World (2.3)

Elmo's finding: Items render in a flat list, no visual divider. Cross-check against 41 pains: Not mentioned. Patrik never complained about separators in a dropdown. Verdict: INVENTED. Steve's spec over-specified the layout. Visual breathing room (padding) is fine. A mandatory borderTop was my preference. Action: Discard the separator requirement. Bobby can use padding, not a forced border.

FAIL #2: Active world indicator is 6px dot, not checkmark (2.4)

Elmo's finding: Small green dot instead of checkmark icon. Cross-check against 41 pains: Not explicitly mentioned. Patrik said "current world (checkmark)" -- Elon confirmed this was descriptive notation, not a UI spec. Verdict: INVENTED (partially). The REAL requirement -- from the design standard -- is "unmistakable active indicator." A 6px dot fails that bar. But the specific widget (checkmark vs filled circle vs badge) is implementation detail. Action: Bobby shipped a checkmark anyway. Keep it. For future specs: spec the outcome ("clearly visible"), not the widget.

FAIL #3: Font sizes below 16px throughout dropdown (4.2)

Elmo's finding: Labels 13px, world names 12px, section headers 10px, slugs 10px. Cross-check against 41 pains: REAL. The 16px minimum comes from the AOM design standard ("old people can read em, young people love em"). This is also directly tied to Pain #10 (spacing/visual quality), Pain #13 (text too long under agent name), and Pain #14 (pills/layout on iPad). 16px is a standing system-wide requirement -- not an Elmo invention. Verdict: REAL. Fix is mandatory before self-serve. Fix: Every text element in world switcher dropdown: 16px minimum body. 14px for secondary (slugs, section headers). Nothing below 14px.

FAIL #4: Touch targets under 44px (4.3)

Elmo's finding: Main items ~36px, world list items ~34px. Cross-check against 41 pains: REAL. Pain #5 (iPhone can't type at half drawer) and Pain #14 (pills too big on iPad, wrong layout) both reflect Patrik's iPhone + iPad usage daily. 44px minimum is the iOS Human Interface Guideline -- it's also in the AOM design standard. Verdict: REAL. Fix is mandatory before self-serve. Fix: minHeight: 44px with display: flex; alignItems: center on all three button types.

FAIL #5: iOS back gesture navigates away (5.4)

Elmo's finding: No popstate listener, no history entry pushed on open. Back gesture closes the whole dashboard. Cross-check against 41 pains: REAL. Pain #5 (iPhone can't type at half drawer), Pain #6 (first drawer not showing), Pain #19 (file upload failing on iPhone) -- all show Patrik hits iOS-specific issues constantly. Back gesture is muscle memory on iPhone. This would bite him every single time. Verdict: REAL. Fix is mandatory before demo (Patrik will swipe back during the demo walkthrough). Fix: Push history entry on dropdown open. popstate listener closes dropdown.

FAIL #6: No keyboard navigation on dropdown (6.1)

Elmo's finding: No arrow key nav, no Escape close. Cross-check against 41 pains: NOT mentioned. Pain #36 is the hotkeys spec (C/B/G/P/F/T + arrow keys to switch agents) -- but that's about the main dashboard, not dropdowns. Verdict: INVENTED (mostly). Escape-to-close is a valid UX best practice and 2 lines of code. Arrow key navigation across dropdown items is out of scope for AOM's target buyer (GCs don't use keyboard-first UIs). Action: Escape close is optional nice-to-have. Arrow nav: trash.

FAIL #7: Create World doesn't show onboarding preview (3.4)

Elmo's finding: Creates account silently, no client-experience preview. Cross-check against 41 pains: NOT mentioned. Patrik asked for the world switcher (Pain #28) -- not for a "preview client onboarding from within the switcher" feature. Verdict: INVENTED. Steve added this to the spec because it seemed valuable for sales demos. It's a legitimate future feature but was never asked for. Action: Trash from current spec. The "Reset & test onboarding" button already handles Patrik previewing his own onboarding. Client-experience preview is a C5/C6 feature.

FAIL #8: Low contrast secondary text (4.7)

Elmo's finding: #334155 on near-black background -- essentially invisible. Cross-check against 41 pains: REAL. Pain #4 (white backgrounds) has 6 mentions -- Patrik is highly contrast-sensitive. He chases low-contrast text as hard as he chases white backgrounds. "Old people can read em" is the standing bar. Verdict: REAL. Fix is mandatory before self-serve. Fix: #64748B minimum for secondary text on dark backgrounds. #94A3B8 preferred.

FAIL #9: No separator between Preferences and Create World (listed again in blockers)

Already covered in FAIL #1 above -- INVENTED.

Section C: Priority Sort for Bobby

Ship before any demo (sales blockers):

  1. Pain #4 -- White backgrounds. Six mentions. If a prospect sees white glass in the AOM expand menu during a demo, we lose them. Zero tolerance.
  2. Pain #7 -- RNB pill colors. The colored pill system IS the pitch. If pills are all orange, the "24/7 AI team" story collapses visually. Fix before any screenshot is taken.
  3. Pain #1 + #2 -- RNB cut off + input stacking. Patrik demos on iPhone. If the demo device shows a broken layout, the sale is over.
  4. Pain #31 -- Can't mark task complete. Basic functionality. If Patrik can't check off a task during a demo, it undermines the whole pitch.
  5. Pain #6 -- First drawer not showing on load. First impression. Prospect clicks an agent room, nothing happens. Immediate credibility hit.

Ship before self-serve (product gates):

  • World switcher: 4 real fixes (fonts 16px, touch targets 44px, contrast, iOS back gesture)
  • Pain #8 -- Drag-and-drop
  • Pain #9 -- Right-click menus wired to actions
  • Pain #19 -- iPhone file upload
  • Pain #20 -- Files tab on mobile + MD viewer

Nice-to-have (ship when capacity allows):

  • Pain #34 -- Description truncation
  • Pain #35 -- "Web" label with green badge
  • Pain #36 -- Hotkeys
  • Pain #38 -- Trello horizontal scroll

Section D: What Needs a New Elmo QA Pass

The world switcher was Elmo's only run. These features have shipped but never been QA'd:

  1. RNB + HUD layout on iPhone (pains #1, #2, #3, #40) -- screenshot-based QA at half drawer and full drawer
  2. Typing indicators (pain #26) -- confirm personality phases show correctly at 30s/120s thresholds
  3. Auth flow / login loop (pain #18) -- incognito test, new account, confirm no password-reset redirect
  4. File upload on iPhone (pain #19) -- live device test needed
  5. Pill color system (pain #7) -- trigger all 5 states (fuchsia/orange/yellow/green/red) and screenshot each

These should be Elmo's next 5 QA passes. I'll write the specs.

Summary

Category Count
Elmo FAIL items that are REAL (Patrik's words or design standard) 4
Elmo FAIL items that are INVENTED (Steve's additions) 4
Elmo FAIL items that are PARTIALLY real 1 (active indicator -- real requirement, invented widget)
Pains with ZERO Elmo QA coverage 22
Pains confirmed FIXED 9
Pains partially fixed 9
Pains still broken 10

Bottom line: Elmo's world switcher pass found 4 real fixes. The other 5 were my over-specification. The broader 41 pains have 10 confirmed still-broken items, only one of which (world switcher) has had any QA run at all. The next priority is QA specs for the 5 high-risk features listed in Section D.
